tenders.title: Radon Measurement Device Evaluation 2026 - 2031
tenders.buyer: Department of Health (HC)
tenders.summary: Health Canada requires services to ensure that radon measurement devices available in Canada are evaluated for their performance on an annual basis.
tenders.text: radon measurement device evaluation 2026 - 2031 health canada requires services to ensure that radon measurement devices available in canada are evaluated for their performance on an annual basis. this is to ensure that any new entrants to the marketplace are evaluated within a reasonable timeframe to ensure they meet minimum performance standards. as a result of this service the vendor will produce a series of publicly available consumer reports on commercially available electronic radon testing devices to ensure the findings of these tests are communicated with consumers. health canada will use the information to review testing guidelines, recommendations and protocols. the scope of this work encompasses the development and ongoing administration of a performance evaluation and testing program for radon measurement devices commercially available to canadian consumers. the work must be designed to assess device performance under conditions that reflect how residents would realistically deploy and use such devices in their homes, ensuring that test results are representative of actual indoor radon activity concentrations.

tenders.text: tsps - 2. business consulting change management services - evaluation of wage's components - interviews, surveys and case studies for the evaluation of wage’s components under the federal 2slgbtqi+ action plan the objective of this requirement is to obtain professional evaluation services to conduct key informant interviews, a survey of funded recipients and unfunded applicants, and case studies in support of the evaluation of women and gender equality canada (wage)’s components under the federal 2slgbtqi+ action plan (2022–23 to 2025–26). the purpose of this evaluation is to assess the extent to which wage has achieved its intended outcomes, drawing on several years of implementation. this evaluation adopts a summative approach to generate evidence on program relevance, implementation and governance, effectiveness and sustainability, and efficiency. the evaluation plan was presented to wage pmec in june 2026. it will focus on the period from 2022–23 to 2025–26 and includes a combination of lines of evidence to ensure the robustness and credibility of findings. in particular, the lines of evidence covered by this statement of work are the key informant interviews, survey and case studies to support accountability and inform future decision-making by identifying key results, lessons learned, and areas for improvement to strengthen ongoing and future programming.

tenders.summary: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) has a requirement to strengthen our existing understanding of effective, properly scoped, monitoring objectives for both macroplastics and microplastics via freshwater monitoring strategies; identify…
tenders.text: science-policy frameworks for nationally coordinated, place-based freshwater macroplastics & microplastics monitoring in canada environment and climate change canada (eccc) has a requirement to strengthen our existing understanding of effective, properly scoped, monitoring objectives for both macroplastics and microplastics via freshwater monitoring strategies; identify fit-for-purpose monitoring approaches aligned with relevant sources, pathways and distribution across key environmental compartments (surface water, sediment, biota); and consider feasibility within current analytical and operational constraints. the work will leverage existing and widely recognized methods and initiatives from regional, national and international sources, where appropriate, to improve consistency, comparability, interoperability, reliability, and efficiency, while minimizing duplication of effort. see annex statement of work in bid solicitation for details.

tenders.buyer: National Research Council of Canada (NRC)
tenders.summary: NRC’s Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Center performs cryogenic research to support its astronomical instrumentation program.
tenders.text: purchase of one (1) general-purpose laboratory vacuum vessel nrc’s herzberg astronomy and astrophysics research center performs cryogenic research to support its astronomical instrumentation program. to support the development of cryogenic instrumentation, it is beneficial to test mechanisms at cryogenic temperatures to verify their performance and lifetime. to enable this testing, nrc is building a test cryostat to allow custom and commercial cryogenic mechanisms to be tested thoroughly prior to use in an instrument. this vacuum vessel will be integrated with a cryocooler, vacuum pump, and other custom parts to create this new cryogenic testing capability.

tenders.title: Laboratory-Scale Gas Atomizer
tenders.buyer: National Research Council of Canada (NRC)
tenders.summary: The National Research Council of Canada (NRC) is seeking the supply, delivery, and installation of a laboratory-scale Gas Atomizer (GA) to enhance powder synthesis activities at the Clean Energy Innovation (CEI) facility in Mississauga.
tenders.text: laboratory-scale gas atomizer the national research council of canada (nrc) is seeking the supply, delivery, and installation of a laboratory-scale gas atomizer (ga) to enhance powder synthesis activities at the clean energy innovation (cei) facility in mississauga. at the cei-mississauga facility, the development and production of advanced battery materials is one of the core activities. high-quality, spherical metal and alloy powders are crucial in advancing the research on energy materials. obtaining powders with precise alloy compositions, particle sizes, morphologies, and quality in small quantities from commercial sources poses significant challenges. to address this issue, nrc intends to procure a ga capable of preparing molten alloys with specific compositions and atomizing them using high-speed gas to produce spherical and fine powders.

tenders.summary: The High Temperature Materials Group in the Structures and Materials Performance Laboratory of the National Research Council’s (NRC) Aerospace (AERO-SMPL-HTM) requires an active vibration isolation (AVI) system to achieve the required performance of the…
tenders.text: active vibration isolation system compatible with a thermo fisher scientific verios 5 ultra high resolution scanning electron microscope (uhr-sem) the high temperature materials group in the structures and materials performance laboratory of the national research council’s (nrc) aerospace (aero-smpl-htm) requires an active vibration isolation (avi) system to achieve the required performance of the group’s ultra-high resolution scanning electron microscope (uhr-sem). aero-smpl-htm uses its uhr-sem in advanced research on a wide range of materials for various applications. however, the instrument cannot provide the highest possible image resolution due to significant low-frequency disturbances during high-magnification imaging. a new avi system will effectively dampen mechanical vibrations and eliminate disruptive low-frequency vibration noise that interferes with image acquisition. the new system will allow the uhr-sem to achieve its optimum performance, and enhance aero-smpl’s capability to conduct advanced research and provide data for a large number of the research projects.

tenders.text: phytoremediation at the eureka high arctic weather station (haws) the eureka high arctic weather station (haws) is situated in an isolated location on the north side of slidre fjord at the northwestern tip of fosheim peninsula, ellesmere island at approximately 80° n. the facility occupies a federal crown-indigenous relations and northern affairs canada (cirnac) land reserve, #1021, spanning an area of 2.23 ha. originally constructed primarily to conduct research in climatology and meteorology, the facility is owned and operated by meteorological service of canada (msc) and has been in operation since april 7th, 1947. the haws is located within in the nunavut settlement area, part of the 350,000 km2 land claim granted to the nunavut inuit in 1993 but excluded from devolution. although remote, the eureka haws is a hub of activity for eccc, the department of national defence (dnd), the polar continental shelf project (pcsp), and the polar environment atmospheric research lab (pearl), to name a few. there are some areas of soil impacted with phcs at the haws that cannot be excavated due to proximity to on-site infrastructure (e.g., buildings, pipelines) or due to risks associated with embankment stability and erosion. these areas present an opportunity for applying an alternative, low-carbon, green remedial approach. phytoremediation is significantly less energy-intensive, more economical and requires minimal operation and maintenance than most conventional remedial methods which rely heavily on the use of heavy machinery. although a proven te

tenders.text: design, installation, maintenance and support of electronic security systems given the evolving threat environment both in canada and internationally, nrcan is focused on strengthening the physical security posture of its facilities. this includes improving access control, surveillance, and intrusion detection capabilities to ensure personnel safety and operational continuity. nrcan operates an electronic security and surveillance system consisting of access control, video management, and intrusion detection systems deployed across multiple locations nationwide. the system is maintained through a combination of in-house it and security resources, as well as contracted security system support and integration services. the system transitioned from legacy analog infrastructure to an ip-based architecture between 2016 and 2020, with ongoing enhancements through 2023. the current security system is built on a hybrid cloud and on-premises architecture, designed to balance cost and performance with confidentiality, integrity, and availability requirements. the system includes approximately 500 card readers and 500 cameras across more than 25 sites and is monitored through the nrcan security operations control centre (socc) located at 580 booth street in ottawa, ontario.

tenders.summary: The National Research Council’s (NRC) Flight Research Laboratory (FRL) operates a Convair 580 aircraft for flight research.
tenders.text: engineering services and support related to the convair 580 aircraft the national research council’s (nrc) flight research laboratory (frl) operates a convair 580 aircraft for flight research. as the aircraft is frequently modified and/or operated in a manner different to the original design purpose, engineering support from the holder of the aircraft’s type design and intellectual property is frequently required. as a result, the frl requires a 5-year standing offer to provide engineering services and support related to the convair 580 aircraft. this work will involve: order of raw materials, machining of raw materials for hardpoint and pylon, engineering studies and/or modifications to the convair 580 to support external sensors, on-going maintenance/repair and technical support, engineering analysis for flight loads, aerodynamics, flight test, component manufacture and/or provision of design/manufacturing data to nrc, pylon completion, fit out, finishing and procurement of additional components/parts necessary for continued operation of the convair 580. additional services/parts not listed may be required to support the modification of the convair 580.

tenders.text: subscription to metal and minerals economic data. the department of natural resources canada (nrcan) has a requirement to provide senior management with detailed and accurate information on gold, silver, platinum group metals (pgms), and other precious metals, including price forecasts; projections on supply and demand components; scenario outlooks for precious metals markets; detailed information about gold mine operations and gold markets; and other relevant information. nrcan will require access to a subscription to proprietary precious-metals market intelligence, historical data, forecasts, investment analysis, and gold mine cost data covering gold, silver, platinum, palladium, rhodium, and related precious-metals markets. the work will involve conducting thorough, data-driven research and sound economic analysis of the gold, silver, pgms, and other precious metals markets and produce datasets, reports, briefing notes, presentations, and other materials that will help inform policy decisions. nrcan will also require user support as needed for questions surrounding the data, the web-based platform, and plug-ins and other online tools if available within three (3) business days.

tenders.text: irb horizon tbips the objective of this requirement is to provide professional services support to the chief innovation and technology office (cito) to advance the modernization of the irb’s case management and adjudicative support environment through the horizons initiative. under this umbrella, work may include a portfolio of related digital modernization projects intended to improve operational efficiency, service quality, sustainability, interoperability, security, and scalability. this work includes initiatives to modernize legacy recording and information-handling capabilities through more current digital approaches; to streamline the creation, organization, and management of electronic case files through increased automation and standardization; and to support structured digital tools that guide and assist decision-making workflows in a more consistent and efficient manner. collectively, these projects are intended to help the irb assess, design, validate, and implement modern digital solutions that reduce manual effort, support more resilient operations, and strengthen the organization’s transition toward a more integrated digital environment.

tenders.summary: Health Canada (HC) evaluates the risks to human health and the environment associated with the use of pesticides and regulates pesticide products in Canada under the Pest Control Products Act.
tenders.text: collection of surface water samples and ancillary data for the canadian water monitoring program for pesticides in priority ontario watersheds. health canada (hc) evaluates the risks to human health and the environment associated with the use of pesticides and regulates pesticide products in canada under the pest control products act. in the interest of increasing the availability of real-world data for use in pesticide risk assessments, hc coordinates the canadian water monitoring program for pesticides (cwmpp). as part of this program, water samples are analysed to determine the concentrations of pesticides present in canadian waters. federal laboratories will analyse approximately 200 chemicals (i.e., pesticide active ingredients and transformation products) in water from various regions across canada. ancillary data and expert advice assist in improving our collective understanding of any patterns observed or any potential levels of concern.

tenders.buyer: Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC)
tenders.summary: Please return offers by email to solicitation-demandedesoumission@cnsc-ccsn.gc.ca Canada is seeking offers from qualified Offerors to provide professional services to review if and how thermal risk assessments (TRAs) are being conducted across the electrical…
tenders.text: thermal releases: review of international regulatory practices and options for incorporation into a compliance and licensing framework. please return offers by email to solicitation-demandedesoumission@cnsc-ccsn.gc.ca canada is seeking offers from qualified offerors to provide professional services to review if and how thermal risk assessments (tras) are being conducted across the electrical power generation industry domestically and internationally, and if there are any existing regulatory frameworks addressing management of thermal effluent. the work will identify gaps in the standardized application of tra methods and provide recommendations where applicable for improvement in standardization of tras for the nuclear power plants in canada. the scope includes a critical evaluation of thermal effects literature for reliability and relevance for being able to inform a tra, and the generation of an updated database of thermal effects thresholds for canadian relevant species fish, and invertebrate species in the marine and freshwater environment. the scope of this project also includes reviewing and compiling data on regulatory approaches used by different facilities utilizing once-through cooling system technology (e.g., nuclear power plants, oil and gas plants, etc.), nationally and internationally, with respect to thermal risk assessment and the derivation and application of thermal thresholds.

tenders.summary: The National Research Council on behalf of the Government of Canada (GoC) and its’ Partners seek to procure a secure, scalable, bilingual web-based digital platform (“the platform”) to support the reporting, review, analysis, and visualization of embodied…
tenders.text: web-based platform for whole building life cycle analysis (wblca) and embodied carbon emissions in building and infrastructure construction the national research council on behalf of the government of canada (goc) and its’ partners seek to procure a secure, scalable, bilingual web-based digital platform (“the platform”) to support the reporting, review, analysis, and visualization of embodied carbon emissions in building and infrastructure construction projects. this procurement includes the design, development, configuration, deployment and ongoing support of the platform. the solution will provide a centralized system that ensure consistent data collection, automated validation, and reporting in alignment with embodied carbon disclosure and reduction policies for buildings and infrastructure projects. at a minimum, the platform shall enable: - intake of material and project specific embodied carbon submissions; - import and export capabilities for compatible whole building life cycle assessment (wblca) submission reports and raw data; - dashboards and customizable reporting functions for internal analysis; and - the creation of an anonymized public dataset. the platform must comply with government of canada security requirements for protected a information and meet canadian-based data residency requirements.

tenders.text: immigration and refugee board of canada - interpreter program the immigration and refugee board of canada (irb) is canada's largest independent administrative tribunal. it is responsible for making well-reasoned decisions on immigration and refugee matters, efficiently, fairly and in accordance with the law. the irb decides, among other responsibilities, who needs refugee protection among the thousands of claimants who come to canada annually. every year, the board renders thousands of decisions on refugee protection and immigration matters. at these hearings, refugees and immigrants who are not fluent in english or french count on the irb to provide them with interpretive services. these interpretive services are required in a wide variety of languages and dialects, reflecting the diverse backgrounds of the refugees and immigrants who come to canada. in order to manage the interpretive services required for such a large number of hearings, including urgent hearings, irb issues contracts to interpreters who provide services on an “as-and-when-requested” basis and invoice for any services they provide. all interpreters are paid the same flat hourly rate. these contracts effectively work as a “roster” of potential interpreters who could be called upon to provide interpretive services at a hearing. selection for contract award: when selecting an applicant for a contract, the irb will consider several factors including the following: • the fluctuation of language demand with respect to immigration trends from specific regions. • previous in
